Draws the reflections of the two sprite fighters' feet in the floor (reached through $085B from draw_fighters). Each fighter is three sprites wide; for the lowest three of each it copies rows 3-10, upside down, into rows 11-18, each byte passed through the mask table at $0500 (every pixel that is not empty set to %11), so the reflection is a silhouette in one colour. The sprite page is patched into the sixteen LDX and STA operands below: $0176 (the buffer's shape page) plus 3, and 4 more for the second fighter ($4C counts the two).

High byte of LDX $0309,Y: the sprite page the first row of feet is read from (patched at $F164). The $03 in the image is a placeholder; every one of the sixteen operands from here to $F1E1 is patched before the loop runs.

High byte of the second LDX: the sprite page of the second row read (patched at $F16A).
High byte of the second STA: where the second reflected row goes (patched at $F167).
High byte of the third LDX (patched at $F170).
High byte of the third STA (patched at $F16D).
High byte of the fourth LDX (patched at $F176).
High byte of the fourth STA (patched at $F173).

High byte of the fifth STA (patched at $F179).

High byte of the eighth STA (patched at $F18B).
The nine byte columns of a fighter's three lowest sprites side by side: offsets 0, 1, 2 in the first shape, $40-$42 in the second, $80-$82 in the third.

Reached only by the BNE at $F221 when the protection check fails: PLP, then JMP ($00A9) through zero page, which sends the program into the weeds. The entry point $F1F9 starts inside this JMP: its operand bytes $A9 $00 are LDA #$00.

Entry, through $0855, called from next_step: the reflection of the third fighter, the one drawn in the floor's characters. Clears characters $F0-$F8 ($5780-$57C7). Then a protection check: with Y left at $FF, LDA $000C,Y reads $010B, a byte the loader leaves there, and LSR and EOR #$51 must give 0 ($A2 or $A3), or it jumps to $F1F7. Then, when place_char_fighter has recorded a bottom row of cells ($01C5 cells, starting at column $01C6 of the fighter's nine, first character $01C7), copies each cell's eight bytes upside down through the mask table $0500 into the character $F0 plus its column, the characters place_char_fighter puts in the row below the feet.

Mode 5, the bonus round, reached through $089D from the main loop. Draws the ball into the six ball shapes, then for each human player in turn (player 2 first, $67): flashes their fist icon, clears the seven slots, sets the launch rate ($FD90 $80, $FD91 0) and the weight of new balls ($FD9B $0C), puts the player in shield move 3 and the shield on its floor ($72), gives the third fighter's colour ($0133, kept in $FD95) the player's colour, fills the floor's colours ($084F) and turns the round on ($8F, so the frame NMI runs $F420). Then each step: reads the joystick ($F840), draws the player in the floor's characters ($0864, $085E), shows message $16 (DEFLECT BALLS FOR 100 POINTS EACH OR AVOID THEM!) once, and waits for the next step ($08A0). A player hit by a ball ($91) falls with the move in $FD94 and the step goes on until no ball is left; one who lasts until all 64 balls are thrown ($8D) and gone ($8E) gets the survival bonus: 50 hundred points ($018A, and $019B for the message's number) and message $15, SURVIVAL BONUS OF 5000 POINTS. After both, waits $78 frames, restores the third fighter's colour and the places ($F3CC), turns the round off, clears the ball shapes and returns to mode 1 through the RTS at $CC9F.

Sets all three fighters to pose $4B and X $B0, the shield's Y to $6A, clears the judge's message ($81 = $FF through $084C) and draws two steps ($087F, $0888, $08A0), then fills the floor's colours ($084F). Called at the start and the end of the bonus round.
Shows message A in the judge's bubble, waits $78 frames, then clears it.

Called by the frame NMI through $0876; does nothing unless the bonus round is on ($8F). Rubs out the balls' spots ($F7E3), then for each slot, 6 down to 0, that is in use ($E2), counting the balls in $8E: slot 6, the shield, only moves. A ball not yet deflected (flag bit 1) that touches the shield (both sprites' bits in the collision latch $01A6, $F51E) while its X is from $4A to $6F is deflected: when the shouts are on, the effects $42 and $43, effect 2's note raised by half the balls thrown and the frame counter ($F0FF), and $010E set so no bounce sound cuts it off; its flags become $13, its horizontal speed is reversed ($F61A) and the player gets 1 hundred points ($018A, through $0897). A ball touching the picture (its bit in the sprite-to-background latch $01A5, $F525) hits the player: the shield is thrown (weight $24, floor $74, up at $FFC0 and sideways by the player's facing, $F52E and $F530), the ball stops falling, and the player's fall move ($F52C, $FD94) is picked by whether the ball came from in front or behind; a ball that touches a player already down only has its vertical speed reversed. Then the ball moves ($F555), takes its colour ($F532) and redraws its reflection ($F7A5). Last, once message $16 has been shown, a new ball may be thrown ($F63E) and the spots are put back ($F7DE).
For each ball slot, the collision bits of its sprite and the shield's (sprite 6): $41, $42, $44, $48, $50, $60, then $FF.
For each ball slot, its sprite's bit in the sprite-to-picture collision latch: 1, 2, 4, 8, $10, $20, then $FF.
The move a player hit by a ball falls with: $11 or $12, by whether the ball came from in front or behind.
The thrown shield's horizontal speed, high byte, by the player's facing: $00 or $FF, with the low bytes at $F530 making +$40 or -$40.
The thrown shield's horizontal speed, low byte: $40 or $C0.
Sets a ball's colour ($EA,X): a ball flagged $20 flashes black and white with bit 2 of its X; otherwise the slot's colour from $F54D.
The two colours of a flashing ball: black and white.
Each slot's colour: black, grey, yellow, green, light blue, white, and black for the shield.

Moves ball X: its vertical speed ($A2 low, $AA high) gains its weight ($D2) and is added to its height ($92 fraction, $9A). At its floor ($DA) it bounces: the effects $40 and $41 when the shouts are on and $010E has run out, the height reflected about the floor, the vertical speed reversed ($F608). Then by its flags ($E2): bit 4 halves the vertical speed once ($F62C) and is cleared; with bit 5 a bounce without bit 4 doubles the speed and sets it, so such a ball bounces low and high in turn. Bits 3 and 2 (halve the vertical, or the horizontal, speed at every bounce) are tested but nothing sets them. Above its floor, anything $6A or lower on the screen is cleared (only the thrown shield, whose floor is lower, gets there). Then its X moves by its horizontal speed ($CA fraction, $C2); at $AB or more, off either side, it is cleared.
Negates ball X's vertical speed ($A2/$AA).
Negates ball X's horizontal speed ($CA/$C2).
Halves ball X's vertical speed, keeping its sign.
Halves ball X's horizontal speed, keeping its sign.

Throws the next ball when it is time, unless the player is down ($91). The timer $FD92/$FD93 grows by the launch rate until its high byte reaches $20. Then it takes the highest free slot of 0-5 (none free: try again next frame); after 64 balls ($8C) it sets $8D instead. The ball gets the weight $FD9B (which grows by one a ball up to $38), floor $56, a starting height picked at random from $F715, flags 1, the launch rate as its speed, and starts at the left (X 4) or, reversed, at the right (X $AA). The rate grows by 8 a ball until it passes $100 plus this bonus round's limit ($F725 by $FDA1). A ball in a slot at or above this round's $F71D gets flags $31 instead: it flashes, starts $20 or $30 high, and bounces low and high in turn.
Starting heights of a new ball, picked by the frame counter and the raster line: $20, $30, $40, $20, $30, $40, $20, $20.
By bonus round ($FDA1 AND 7), the lowest slot whose balls are thrown with flags $31: 6, 6, 5, 6, 4, 6, 2, 6 (slot 6 is never thrown, so 6 means none).
By bonus round, the low byte the launch rate stops growing at once its high byte is 1: $80, $80, $C0, $C0, $E0, $E0, $F0, $FF.

Twenty-two blank bytes, then the ball at $F743, which is the same upside down: a ball's reflection is copied from here into rows 10-20 of its sprite, starting further back the higher the ball is ($F79A).
The ball, ten rows of two bytes (16 pixels wide), drawn into rows 0-9 of each ball sprite by $F763.
Where each ball slot's sprite shape is, low bytes: $58C0, $5900, $5940, $5980, $59C0, $5A00.
The ball shapes' addresses, high bytes.
Draws the ball from $F743 into the top ten rows of each of the six ball shapes.
Clears the ball shapes, $58C0-$59BF and $59C0-$5ABF.

For a ball 0 to 10 pixels above its floor, where in $F72D its reflection starts: $16 at the floor and four less (two rows) for each pixel up, so as the ball's sprite rises one row the reflection moves two rows down inside it, one row down on the screen, as in a mirror; from 6 pixels up it starts at 0, all blank.

Redraws the reflection in rows 10-20 of ball $90's shape when the ball is in use and less than eleven pixels above its floor ($DA less $9A); $F7B6 is the entry that blanks it, used when a ball is thrown.
Entry of ball_reflection_draw with A = $0A: draws the blank rows from $F72D, so a thrown ball starts with no reflection.
Draws each ball's spot at the place its X gives ($F810), so the balls seem to roll. $F7E3 is the entry that rubs the spots out (A = 0 takes the plain bytes from $F830).
Entry of ball_spots_on with A = 0: puts the plain bytes from $F830 back, rubbing each ball's spot out before it moves.
Byte offsets round the ball's outline for each of 16 steps of its X: the spot travels round.
